EMILDAI sits at the crossroads of law, data protection and AI, offered by six partner universities led from Avignon. Applications for the 2027/2029 editions open in November 2026; the previous round closed on 25 January 2026, a date the new cycle is expected to mirror.

Programme Highlights

  • Six-university consortium at the law-AI-data interface
  • November 2026 opening with a late-January closing pattern
  • Study tracks in data governance, AI law and cybersecurity
  • Graduates enter privacy offices, AI-regulation roles and tech policy

Who Should Apply

Law and computing graduates are both admitted, with study tracks designed for each stream; the consortium values interdisciplinary motivation.

Funding and Costs

Scholarships for the first round: partial fee waivers and EMJM-funded places depending on the edition.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply on the EMILDAI site once the November window opens and target the late-January scholarship deadline. Key deadline information: 25 January 2027 (expected — applications open November 2026; the 2026-2028 round closed 25 January 2026).

Official Source

  • Official application page (verified link)

About EMILDAI Consortium (Avignon Université)

The EMILDAI consortium is coordinated by Avignon Université and delivers the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Law, Data and Artificial Intelligence with six European partner universities.

Official website: https://emildai.eu

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 25 January 2027 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
